title: Activation Lighthouse: Canary & Telemetry Lab Notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose
This is a working lab doc for the Activation Lighthouse concept: a small, cross-functional ops pattern combining a lightweight canary, telemetry lighthouse probes, and an A/B hypothesis canvas.

Audience
- Product owners, experiment owners
- Release engineers / SREs
- Observability / telemetry
- Solutions & SEs who run customer rollouts

Status
- Draft / lab notes. Not approved as the canonical rollout playbook.
- Goal: converge on a minimal safe pattern we can reuse for medium-risk LLM feature rollouts where model selection, routing, or cost controls matter.

Quick summary / TL;DR (for oncall)
- Launch a 1%–5% canary slice with synthetic probe traffic + real-user sampling.
- Drive a short lived telemetry lighthouse run (6–12 hours) to validate critical signals: latency P50/P95, request error rate, cost per token, and prompt-quality regression metric.
- If any hard guardrails fail, automatically shift canary traffic off and route to stable baseline.

Core components (working definitions)
- Canary slice: a targeted traffic cohort (by region, user cohort, or route) sized for operational detection, not full statistical power. Typical: 1% global or a single geo with 5–10k requests/hr.
- Telemetry lighthouse: a curated set of synthetic probes and fast-running checks designed to exercise known failure modes quickly (prompt-edge cases, long-sequence scenarios, retry storms).
- Hypothesis canvas: one-line hypothesis + metric list + acceptance/reject criteria. Each canary must attach a canvas.

Hypothesis canvas (template)
- Hypothesis: "Switching to model-X for /generate/ will reduce median latency by >= 10% without increasing hallucination score by > 2pp."
- Primary success metric(s): latency_p50 (ms), hallucination_rate (prompt-quality-%), relative_cost_per_1k_tokens ($).
- Guardrail metrics: p95 latency, error_rate (5xx), user_facing_timeouts, model-fallback-rate.
- Acceptance: primary metric meets target AND no guardrail exceeds threshold for 6 continuous hours.
- Reject: any hard guardrail breach or sustained degradation for >15 minutes without self-healing.

Operational checklist (pre-canary)
- Owner assigned and pager informed (owner, backfill).
- Hypothesis canvas uploaded to experiment board (link in linked_artifacts).
- Synthetic probes defined (input set + expected patterns).
- Canary cohort selected and traffic weighting plan documented.
- Fallback route confirmed + automated fallback policy in routing layer.
- Observability dashboard created: short list of slices and alert rules.
- Runbook quick actions documented (rollback, scale-down, throttles).

Telemetry lighthouse probes (examples)
- Latency probe: 50 short prompts, 10 long prompts (>= 1024 tokens) in succession. Check p50/p95 and token emission rate.
- Failure injection: simulate transient GPU OOM on a replica to verify graceful fallback to faster model variant.
- Cost probe: send batched low-volume requests to measure batching behavior and token accounting.
- Semantic probe: 100 canned prompts with known expected surface responses; compute prompt-quality-score (fuzzy matching + human-labeled baseline).

Fast safety thresholds (defaults, tuned per product)
- Hard guardrails (immediate): error_rate > 0.5% absolute increase vs baseline (10m window), p95 latency > baseline + 500ms, user_timeouts increase > 0.2pp.
- Soft guardrails (operator review): p50 improvement < 5% or hallucination_score increase 0.5–2pp.
- Cost guardrail: estimated cost_per_1k_tokens increase > 20% without commensurate quality gain.

Alerting & automation
- Short-window alerts (1m spike, 5m sustained) for hard guardrails => trigger automated traffic switch to baseline and page oncall.
- Medium-window alerts (15m–60m) for soft guardrails => notify owners, auto-rollback only with owner approval.
- Post-mortem: Any automated fallback must create an incident stub with minimal triage info.

Sampling and statistical considerations (practical guidance)
- We intentionally do NOT aim for full A/B power in the initial canary. Canary is about safety signals and ops detection.
- For feature experiments requiring product-level lift measurement, run a separate A/B with appropriate sample size and power calculations.
- MDE guidance (for A/B experiments): for conversion-like signals with baseline 2% CTR, to detect 10% relative lift (~0.2pp absolute) at 80% power requires O(100k) users per variant — plan experiments separately.
- Use two-proportion z-test or bootstrap for non-normal metrics. Tag experiments so we can map A/B vs canary cohorts in analytics.

Rollout cadence & escalation matrix
- Phase 0: internal synthetic + alpha users (0–0.1% traffic) — 1–4 hours.
- Phase 1: small canary (1%) with telemetry lighthouse — 6–12 hours observed. If green, continue.
- Phase 2: progressive scale to 5% then 25% over 24–48 hours with staggered checks and smoke tests.
- Phase 3: full release with extended observation windows (72h).

Escalation (who does what)
- Canary owner: owns immediate triage, triggers rollback if hard guardrail tripped and automation didn't.
- Observability engineer: validates alerts and root-cause guesses (telemetry correlation).
- Release eng / SRE: executes hotfix or capacity action.
- Product lead: decides on experiment continuation in case of soft guardrail failures.

Quick runbook snippets (copyable)
- Manual rollback: change route weight to 0% in routing console -> confirm traffic shifts -> monitor key metrics for 5m -> close incident stub.
- Isolate canary cohort: apply traffic-shift rule tagged canary = true -> throttle at ingress -> start synthetic probes.
- Capture traces: enable debug sampling rate to 100% for canary user agents for 10 minutes then revert.

Open questions and tradeoffs (work items)
- How aggressive should auto-fallback be for cost-only regressions? (Ravi to propose policy).
- Can we make the telemetry lighthouse run entirely synthetic to avoid privacy exposure for sensitive customers? Pros/cons: synthetic probes may miss real-user interactions.
- Do we require a human sign-off after the 6–12 hour green window for model changes that affect content quality?

Next steps (action items)
- Create a small standard dashboard template for Activation Lighthouse that teams can clone (Marco).
- Add a checkbox in the rollout ticket template to confirm a lighthouse probe suite is attached (Janelle).
- Draft automated fallback policy mapping (soft vs hard guardrails) and publish for review (Ravi).
- Run 2 internal dry-runs on staging with the lighthouse probes and document outcomes.

Notes to self / rough thoughts
- Keep the canary cohort small enough to limit surface but large enough to see latency and resource issues. Usually geography-based slices reveal infra/network edge cases faster.
- Instrument a small set of prompts as "sentinel prompts" for content regressions — these should be maintained by product owners per vertical.

Links & references
- Experiment run template: confluence:experiment-templates/quick-ab
- Routing & fallback policy draft: github:rw/routing-policy/draft.md

Appendix: example minimal alert rule text
- Name: "Activation-Lighthouse — p95 spike"
- Target: any route tagged candidate-release
- Condition: p95_latency > baseline_p95 + 500ms over 5m with volume > 100 requests
- Response: page oncall -> run automated traffic switch -> create incident draft

End of document.

(This file intentionally keeps phrasing terse. Will iterate after two dry-runs.)
